reply_text:
I found three dated forward-looking lines from Pichai in 2016. All three come from third-party transcripts of Google's own events, and each one is borderline against your rules. I found no 2016 statement from him about when AGI or superintelligence would arrive.

**What I found**
- **Google I/O keynote, 2016-05-18:** "We as Google have evolved significantly over the past 10 years and we believe we are poised to take a big leap forward in the next 10 years." The span is 10 years, but the subject is Google. AI is the context around it, not the thing being predicted.
- **Same keynote:** "we are getting ready to launch something later this year." This is about bringing the Google Assistant into the home, so it is close to a product launch date. The more explicit line, "Google Home will be available later this year," was said by Mario Queiroz, not Pichai, so I left it out.
- **Made by Google, 2016-10-04:** "We'll literally translate billions of queries over the coming year." This is about the new machine-learning translation system for Chinese to English. It is a usage forecast for an AI system, not a spending or revenue one.

**What I left out**
- His best-known 2016 line, "We will move from mobile first to an AI first world," appears in both transcripts and in the April 2016 Founders' Letter. In the transcripts it carries no date. I couldn't check the letter: the Recode copy was blocked, and I didn't use any of my searches to look for another copy, such as the one on abc.xyz. The words "over time" come only from search snippets, so I haven't quoted them as read.

**Mistakes on my part**
- My script read three successful page loads as errors and threw away the text, so I opened one page twice. That cost me the Forbes interview of 2016-05-20 and the CNBC Code Conference report of 2016-06-01. Neither should be counted as checked; I quote nothing from them.
- The I/O transcript I opened seems to stop early. Any closing remarks about AI from Pichai at that keynote were not seen.
- I used 9 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
